key_insight: Correcting only teacher-disfavored tokens in failed student rollouts improves visual mathematical reasoning without full-response imitation or figure descriptions at test time.
engineering_relevance: Training-time perceptual correction can improve smaller vision-language models without requiring additional annotations or model calls at inference.
method: Collect on-policy student rollouts for visual math problems.
Use a teacher with reference figure descriptions and verified solutions to score incorrect rollouts under a minimal-edit objective; apply corrective loss only to teacher-disfavored tokens.
Train correct rollouts with task-reward reinforcement learning.
evidence_signal: Across model scales, the method meets or exceeds description-assisted base models, improves low-level geometric perception, and transfers to external mathematics and perception benchmarks.
watch_item: Training requires reference figure descriptions and verified solutions; a frozen same-size teacher works but yields smaller gains than a larger teacher on most metrics.
paper_title: Edit, Don't Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
